The two defect counts are different measurements. The first is of the declared RACI matrix — activities with no accountable role, or with more
than one. The second is of every step, checklist item and artefact in scope, whose free-text owner is resolved through the role registry. Both are
reported even at zero, because "no defects found" and "not checked" are not the same statement.
Principles, the council charter and the RACI matrix carry no layer tag: they apply to every engagement regardless of the current scope.
Only elements that drive regulatory returns, risk models, board KPIs or P&L are stewarded. Everything else
A large bank holds on the order of a million columns and a few hundred elements that actually matter. Programmes that attempt full coverage
exhaust their sponsor's patience before producing a measurable outcome.
Start at the regulatory return line or board KPI, trace lineage back to source, and every element on that path
Produces a finite, defensible list with immediate business relevance, and avoids an open-ended nomination process that never converges.
The DG Office sets standards, runs tooling and reports. Domains own their data, their definitions and their
Central-only models collapse at the throughput limit of the central team. Federation scales; centralisation queues.
Data Owners are business department heads. IT is custodian — it implements and secures, but does not
decide what a term means or what quality is acceptable.
When IT owns definitions, business disputes are unresolvable because the arbiter has no authority over the disputing parties.
Every policy must name at least one enforcement point — a pipeline test, an approval gate or a control —
Unenforced policy documents are the most common artefact of failed programmes and the least useful.
Stewards are named individuals with a written percentage of time in their formal objectives, countersigned
Unallocated stewardship is the single most reliable predictor of programme failure, and the easiest to eliminate before it happens.
